analysis.investment_thesis: Angel One built an impressive digital broking franchise with a 9-year revenue CAGR of 31.4%, but SEBI's 2024–2025 F&O regulations have structurally disrupted the business model — revenue fell from ₹5,239 Cr to ₹5,137 Cr and net profit plunged from ₹1,172 Cr to ₹915 Cr in 2026, which is the growth deceleration red flag Fisher treated as a sell signal. Borrowings have exploded from ₹788 Cr to ₹7,951 Cr as margin funding scales, adding balance sheet risk.
key_strengths: Large and loyal digital client base built over decades, with a strong tech platform (Super App) that is costly for competitors to replicate
Diversification into credit, insurance, and mutual fund distribution reduces pure F&O revenue dependence over time
9-year operating income CAGR of 103% demonstrates extraordinary business transformation from legacy broker to fintech
key_risks: SEBI's F&O restrictions are structural, not transient — the high-margin derivatives revenue that drove profitability has permanently shrunk
Borrowings up 10x in 4 years (₹788 Cr → ₹7,951 Cr); rising finance costs (₹437 Cr in 2026) compress net margins
Promoter holding of only 28.87% is low — management incentive alignment is weaker than Fisher prefers
red_flags: Net profit declined 22% YoY in 2026 (₹1,172 Cr → ₹915 Cr) — Fisher's clearest sell trigger is decelerating/declining earnings
OCF deeply negative for 3 consecutive years: -₹330 Cr (2024), -₹1,860 Cr (2025), -₹4,142 Cr (2026) — though partly structural for margin-funding operations
ROE at 15.6% is below Fisher's 20% threshold and likely declining as equity base grows faster than profits
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Fisher's Scuttlebutt method would have revealed the regulatory risk to Angel One's model well before it hit the P&L — SEBI's index derivative restrictions were telegraphed publicly, and any industry channel check in 2024 would have flagged the F&O dependency. The platform itself has genuine merit: 20M+ clients, a well-regarded tech stack, and the pivot to lending (margin funding) is a natural adjacency. But lending at scale changes the business model's risk profile fundamentally — credit risk, funding risk, and regulatory risk all increase simultaneously.

Fisher was willing to hold through temporary setbacks, but the 2026 numbers represent more than a blip: revenue is flat, net profit has declined 22%, and the earnings quality has deteriorated. Forward P/E of 20x implies the market expects earnings recovery — if SEBI's framework stabilizes and the credit book performs, that recovery is plausible. But Fisher would require 2–3 quarters of re-accelerating growth and ROE recovery above 20% before adding conviction. For now, this is a watch-and-hold.
